name: Cocoa/hot-chocolate beverage mixes and malted drink powders
anchor: Per-form sovereign beverage cells in the as-consumed liquid basis (EU 2023/915 juice and rice-drink cells, Codex CXS 193 fruit juices, EU 2024/1987 beverage nickel, EU canned-beverage tin, Hong Kong Cap 132V's named carbonated, tea, coffee and wine beverage entries, and the US and Hong Kong packaged-drinking-water quality standards), with dry leaf, bean and powder commodities anchored separately in their own as-sold basis and never converted between the two
cross_reference: Appended to Category 5 to resolve the dangling Category 33 cross-reference. Chocolate confectionery and eating chocolate are NOT in this row: they are a different product form with their own government-written cocoa-solids bands, and they route to the confectionery category.
native_basis_label: dry powder as sold, reported on the as-sold article, which is the basis EU 2023/915 and EU 2024/1987 use for the cocoa-powder cells that bind this row (product as placed on the market)
scope_note: Dry powders sold to be reconstituted into a beverage: unsweetened cocoa powder sold for drinking, sweetened cocoa powder, powdered drinking chocolate and hot-chocolate mixes, and malted drink powders whose characterising ingredient is cocoa or malt. Includes fat-reduced cocoa powder. Excludes eating chocolate and chocolate confectionery, which are a different product form; excludes ready-to-drink chocolate and malted milk beverages, which are liquid dairy or plant drinks and route to Category 24 or the plant-milk rows; excludes any mix carrying a Supplement Facts panel, which routes to Category 16. The row is certified in the as-sold dry powder basis because that is the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples, and because the binding instruments are themselves written in that basis; no reconstitution factor is applied to convert the ceiling into an as-consumed beverage value.
basis_guard: as[ _]sold|product as placed on market|edible part|dry matter|dry weight|portion ordinarily consumed
basis_guard_note: This row publishes a dry-commodity ceiling in the as-sold basis (the article the applicant packages and the lot the auditor samples), so every named anchor must itself be a dry-commodity as-sold or as-placed-on-market cell. The guard refuses the ready-to-drink beverage cells: Hong Kong Cap 132V Note 11 restricts its beverage entries to beverages that are, or are reconstituted to be, ready to drink, and applying a ready-to-drink ceiling to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation in the strict direction, not a standard. This row's guard additionally admits the FSANZ basis phrase (portion ordinarily consumed), which binds the cadmium cell. That phrase denotes the edible portion of the food as listed rather than a prepared serving, so for a powder consumed in its entirety it coincides with the as-sold dry article this row publishes, and no reconstitution or dilution factor is applied. The admission is narrow and row-specific: it is not extended to the other dry rows in this category, none of which has an FSANZ anchor.
method: HMTc Method v2.0 (government-limit-only): the strictest applicable sovereign maximum level for this exact beverage form and analyte in the row's declared native basis, with disclosed read-across where the exact cell is unregulated, a substantiated not-material determination where a species is bounded or is a method artifact, and a control where no defensible sovereign number and no supportable near-neighbour exist. Never occurrence-derived. Ready-to-drink and dry-commodity bases are never mixed and no brewing, dilution or reconstitution factor is invented.

Pb.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a lead maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. This is a real and consequential gap, and it is disclosed rather than filled. EU 2023/915 writes cadmium cells for cocoa powder and for every chocolate cocoa-solids band but no lead cell for any of them; Codex CXS 193, FSANZ Schedule 19, Health Canada and Hong Kong Cap 132V likewise set no lead maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or malted drink powder. The read-across candidates were examined and all rejected: the Hong Kong Milk cell (20 ug/kg) is an as-consumed liquid value and applying it to a dry powder that is reconstituted at roughly one part in ten would be a basis conflation in the strict direction; the sugar cells cover a different, refined commodity that supplies little of a mix's lead; the tea and coffee commodity cells are unrelated botanicals. Lead is the analyte of greatest concern in cocoa supply chains, so this control is written with a hard escalation rule rather than a soft one. Lead is a Tier-1 analyte, so a control here means mandatory lot testing with an escalation rule, not an absence of scrutiny; no ceiling is invented from occurrence data.
Pb.reference_method: Lead by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold basis, reported on the certificate. Any result above 100 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient-origin, milling and equipment investigation and blocks certification pending resolution; results feed the Standards Ratchet trigger pool under Governance Policy section 12.

Cd.basis: dry cocoa or drinking-chocolate powder as sold (edible portion, no reconstitution applied)

stricter_unselected.scope: milk chocolate with less than 30 percent total d
chocolate with less than 50 percent total dry co
Chocolates containing or declaring < 30% total c

Cd.label: Two credible sovereigns write a cadmium cell that reaches this exact product form. FSANZ Schedule 19 sets 500 ug/kg for chocolate AND COCOA PRODUCTS, which covers a drinking-cocoa powder on its face; EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.2.15.4 sets 600 ug/kg for cocoa powder placed on the market for the final consumer or as an ingredient in sweetened cocoa powder or powdered chocolate, which names this row's sweetened and powdered-chocolate mixes explicitly; Hong Kong Cap 132V sets 2000 ug/kg for cocoa powder ready for consumption. All three are named; the FSANZ cell is the strictest applicable and binds.
Cd.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup across three named sovereign cells, taking the strictest applicable rather than the most convenient. The FSANZ cell binds at 500 ug/kg: its scope phrase reaches cocoa products generally rather than confectionery only, so it applies to a drinking-cocoa or hot-chocolate powder without any extension of scope, and it is stricter than the EU cell that names this form most precisely. Its basis, the portion ordinarily consumed, is the edible portion of the food as listed, which for a powder that is consumed in its entirety is the powder as sold; no reconstitution factor is applied, and if the phrase were instead read as the prepared drink the FSANZ ceiling would be an order of magnitude stricter still, so adopting it on the as-sold powder is the conservative reading in the applicant's favour and is disclosed as such. The stricter cells the audit scan flags are all CHOCOLATE CONFECTIONERY bands and are rejected on scope, not on convenience: EU 2023/915 writes a cocoa-solids band structure for chocolate (milk chocolate under 30 percent dry cocoa solids at 100 ug/kg, chocolate under 50 percent at 300 ug/kg, chocolate at or above 50 percent at 800 ug/kg) and Hong Kong writes the same structure (300 to 900 ug/kg), and both drafted those bands alongside a separate, dedicated cell for the drinking powder. Eating chocolate is a different product form, excluded from this row by its own scope note and routed to the confectionery category. Method v2.0 step 4 requires HMTc to preserve the product-form split the government itself wrote rather than to import a confectionery band into a beverage powder because it produces a lower number. Cadmium in cocoa is origin-driven and well characterised, so this cell is a declared Standards Ratchet priority under Governance Policy section 12; occurrence data may inform surveillance but may not select the number.

tAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-arsenic maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. Regulators write beverage arsenic limits on the inorganic species (EU 2023/915 section 3.4.4 fruit juices at 20 ug/kg and section 3.4.1.6 non-alcoholic rice-based drinks at 30 ug/kg; the US FDA apple-juice action level at 10 ug/kg) and write unspeciated arsenic limits only in the packaged-water and public-water-supply schedules, which are Category 8 instruments. No sovereign writes an inorganic-arsenic cell for this commodity either, so both arsenic cells in this row are controls and the escalation rule carries the obligation. Total arsenic is therefore mandatory on every lot as the parent screen and no total-arsenic ceiling is invented.
tAs.reference_method: Total arsenic by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Inorganic-arsenic speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS) is reflexed whenever total arsenic exceeds 50 percent of this row's inorganic-arsenic ceiling, or 20 ug/kg where this row publishes no inorganic-arsenic number. Species never substitute for the total: the iAs result does not satisfy the tAs reporting requirement.

iAs.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an inorganic-arsenic maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. Every sovereign inorganic-arsenic cell is scoped either to rice and rice-based products, to a ready-to-drink beverage (EU fruit juices 20 ug/kg, EU non-alcoholic rice-based drinks 30 ug/kg, US FDA apple juice 10 ug/kg), to seafood, or to packaged and public drinking water. None of those is applicable to this dry commodity, and applying a ready-to-drink beverage cell to a dry leaf, bean or powder would be a basis conflation. Inorganic arsenic is a Tier-1 analyte, so it is speciated whenever the total-arsenic screen is elevated.
iAs.reference_method: Inorganic arsenic by HPLC-ICP-MS, reflexed whenever total arsenic on the lot exceeds 100 ug/kg in the as-sold dry basis; a confirmed inorganic-arsenic result escalates to an origin and irrigation-water investigation. Inorganic arsenic never substitutes for the total-arsenic report.

tHg.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-mercury maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. The sovereign mercury values in this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 total mercury at 2 ug/kg; Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water, written for inorganic mercury at 6 ug/kg) and the fish and seafood methylmercury and total-mercury ceilings, none of which governs this product form. Mercury has no identified enrichment pathway in this supply chain, but the analyte is on the mandatory eight-total panel, so testing is mandatory and no ceiling is invented.
tHg.reference_method: Total mercury by ICP-MS (or dedicated amalgamation AAS) on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. A detection above 5 ug/kg escalates to an ingredient and process-water investigation and reflexes methylmercury speciation.

MeHg.rationale: Methylmercury has no formation pathway in a dry cocoa or malted beverage powder: there is no marine bioaccumulation step in the supply chain and no anaerobic, sulfate-reducing methylation environment in the product or its process. Methylmercury is a component of total mercury (MeHg <= tHg) and is governed by and bounded by the total-mercury cell; no separate methylmercury ceiling is published.
MeHg.reference_method: Bounded by the total-mercury cell (tHg). Methylmercury speciation (HPLC-ICP-MS or GC-ICP-MS) is reflexed only on an elevated total-mercury result; it is not a routine lot test for this form.
MeHg.regulatory_basis: No credible sovereign sets a methylmercury limit for any beverage, leaf, bean or beverage powder. Methylmercury maximum levels are scoped to fish, seafood and other marine matrices (EU 2023/915 section 3.3, US FDA CPG 540.600, Hong Kong Cap 132V fish entries). Methylmercury is a species of and bounded by total mercury (MeHg <= tHg), which this row controls directly.
MeHg.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (and EU 2024/1987 for nickel, EU 2025/1891 for arsenic in seafood); Codex CXS 193-1995; US FDA (21 CFR 165.110 bottled-water quality standards, Juice HACCP guidance, Closer to Zero action levels); FSANZ Food Standards Code Schedule 19; Health Canada List of Contaminants and Other Adulterating Substances; UK retained maximum levels; Hong Kong Cap 132V (Food Adulteration (Metallic Contamination) Regulations) — none sets a methylmercury limit for this product form.

Ni.basis: product as placed on market, dry cocoa or drinking-chocolate powder

stricter_unselected.scope: milk chocolate >= 30 % dry cocoa solids, and cho

Ni.label: EU 2024/1987 sets nickel at 15000 ug/kg for cocoa powder and fat-reduced cocoa powder, and the register row records the instrument's own parenthetical for that cell, drinking chocolate. This is a DIRECT sovereign maximum level for this row's product form and basis and it binds; the cell applies from 1 July 2025.
Ni.substantiation: Direct regulatory lookup. The chocolate nickel bands in the same instrument (milk chocolate under 30 percent dry cocoa solids at 2500 ug/kg, milk chocolate at or above 30 percent and chocolate at 7000 ug/kg) are stricter but are written for eating chocolate, a different product form that this row excludes; adopting one of them because it is lower would be reaching past the instrument's scope, and the EU drafters wrote the cocoa-powder cell at 15000 knowing those bands existed. Cocoa is a genuine nickel accumulator, which is why the EU's own cocoa-powder value is the highest nickel cell in the instrument outside the seaweeds; the number is published as written. Nickel is a Tier-2 analyte.

Sn.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a tin maximum level for a dry cocoa or malted beverage powder. The exclusion is written into the instrument itself: EU 2023/915 Annex I section 3.5 scopes its inorganic-tin maximum levels to canned beverages and canned foods and expressly excepts canned dried and canned powdered products, and the Codex, FSANZ and Hong Kong canned-food cells carry the same carve-out. There is therefore no sovereign number for a dry beverage commodity and no supportable read-across, because the canned-liquid cells are written in a ready-to-drink basis. Tin is nonetheless on the mandatory eight-total panel.
Sn.reference_method: Total tin by ICP-MS on every certified lot in the as-sold dry basis, reported on the certificate. Where the applicant also sells a canned ready-to-drink form of this product, that form is verified separately against the canned-beverage tin maximum level in the as-consumed basis.

Al.rationale: No credible sovereign sets an aluminium maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder, and no near-neighbour read-across is supportable: the only sovereign aluminium values are packaged-drinking-water quality standards written in a litre-of-water basis (Category 8) and the FSANZ infant-formula limits (Category 1). Applying a water-basis value to a dry commodity would be a basis conflation of roughly three orders of magnitude. Aluminium is a live cell for this row: cocoa is grown on acidic tropical soils where plant-available aluminium is elevated, and alkalised (Dutch-process) cocoa carries a processing-aid route as well. Both are investigated on an elevated result.
Al.reference_method: Total aluminium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate in the as-sold dry basis. A result that departs materially from the applicant's own documented origin and process baseline escalates to a soil, cultivar and processing-aid investigation. This is a process-control tripwire, not a numeric standard: no ceiling is published because no credible sovereign maximum exists for this cell.

Cr.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a total-chromium maximum level for cocoa powder, drinking chocolate or a malted drink powder. The only sovereign chromium values reachable from this basis family are the packaged-drinking-water quality standards (US 21 CFR 165.110 at 100 ug/kg, Hong Kong Cap 132V packaged drinking water at 50 ug/kg), which govern water sold as water and are Category 8 instruments, and the public-water-system maximum contaminant levels (US EPA, Health Canada), which are water-utility instruments and not food law at all. Total chromium in this form is dominated by benign Cr(III) and is reported as a stainless-steel equipment and process-water leaching screen, not as a health limit; the health-relevant species is addressed in the Cr-VI cell.
Cr.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot, reported on the certificate. An elevated result triggers the Cr(VI) speciation reflex and an equipment, process-water and ingredient investigation.

Cr-VI.rationale: No credible sovereign sets a hexavalent-chromium limit for any food or beverage, and the in-matrix reduction argument that supports a not-material determination in an acidic beverage is not available here: this row's certified article is a DRY powder, and alkalised cocoa is mildly ALKALINE rather than acidic, which is the condition under which Cr(VI) is most stable rather than least; the acidic-beverage reduction argument is therefore not merely unavailable but pointing the other way. Because Cr(VI) cannot be assumed to be reduced to Cr(III) in this matrix, the fail-safe disposition is a control rather than a not-material determination, and no ceiling is invented.
Cr-VI.reference_method: Total chromium by ICP-MS on every certified lot. Cr(VI)-specific speciation (IC-ICP-MS, EN 15192 adapted) is reflexed whenever total chromium exceeds 100 ug/kg in this form, or 50 percent of the total-chromium screen value where this row publishes one. A confirmed Cr(VI) detection escalates to a process-water, equipment and ingredient investigation and blocks certification pending resolution.
